protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to create a virtual keyboard.
The virtual keyboard is similar to a regular keyboard. However, the client creating the keyboard does not receive the key events. Instead, the compositor will send them to the currently focused client.
The virtual keyboard can be used to implement alternative input methods such as on-screen keyboards.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1
interface.description: A virtual keyboard manager is used to create virtual keyboards.

request.name: create_virtual_keyboard
request.description: This request creates a new virtual keyboard object.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the manager.

interface.name: zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1
interface.description: The virtual keyboard is an object that will be sent to the focused client instead of the real keyboard.

request.name: keymap
request.description: Sets the keymap for the virtual keyboard. This request is sent right after the virtual keyboard is created and has to be sent again if the keymap changes.

request.name: key

description.summary: send key event from virtual keyboard

request.description: Sends a key event from the virtual keyboard to the focused client.

request.name: modifiers
request.description: Sends the current modifiers state to the focused client.

entry.name: no_keymap
entry.summary: no keymap; client will decide what keys do
